clue.text: Head of sales to improve appearance of new business

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the front of sales is used

parts.note: to tart up is to smarten something cheaply

explanation.surface: A sales chief sets about smartening the look of a fledgling company.
explanation.definitionFit: A start-up is a newly founded company, usually small and seeking growth.

clue.text: First of seafaring crew's in boat

indicators.note: only the opening letter of seafaring is used

parts.note: a crew is a team, and the 's makes it possessive, teams'
in means fashionable, hip

explanation.surface: The first of a ship's crew is aboard the vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but means fashionable, HIP; 'crew's' gives TEAMS.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam-powered vessel is a large kind of boat.

clue.text: Brief display on northern island

indicators.note: brief means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: an array is an impressive display

explanation.surface: A short exhibition held on an island in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Arran is an island off the west coast of Scotland, in the Firth of Clyde.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish island in the Firth of Clyde, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Soldiers successfully attacked one Pacific location

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers
to hit a target is to attack it successfully
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Troops have attacked an island in the Pacific with success.
explanation.definitionFit: A French Polynesian island in the South Pacific, an example of a place there.

clue.text: Prudish, like one sort of minister mostly

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a prime minister is one sort of minister

explanation.surface: A minister described as rather straitlaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiffly formal and easily shocked, a near synonym of prudish.

clue.text: Roast meat tasty with ends trimmed

parts.note: lamb is a kind of meat

indicators.note: trimming the ends removes the first and last letters of tasty

explanation.surface: A cook describes a joint of meat, trimmed and tasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roast' looks like the cooking sense, but it is the verb meaning to criticise harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast someone is slang for scolding them severely, a synonym for berating.

clue.text: Fruit squash began to be transported by juggernaut

indicators.note: goods transported by a lorry are carried inside it

parts.note: a juggernaut is a huge lorry, a large truck

indicators.note: squashing something crushes it out of shape, so the letters of began are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soft-drink concentrate set off by lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squash' looks like the fruit drink, which suits the surface, but it is the anagram signal; a juggernaut is a very large lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid of raspberry and blackberry is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Mother less polite about a person involved in 10?

parts.note: ma is mother

indicators.note: about puts the rude word around the letter a

parts.note: ruder means less polite

explanation.surface: Mum is less polite to someone taking part in a raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is the answer to 10 across, RAIDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A raider who roams in search of plunder takes part in sudden attacks.

clue.text: Trade I'm in will collapse temporarily

indicators.note: a collapse leaves things in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A worker fears their trade is about to fail.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase meaning for the meantime, used of interim arrangements.

clue.text: Before end of journey pilot becomes irritable

indicators.note: the pilot word comes before the final letter in this down answer

parts.note: a pilot is a trial run, a test

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An airline pilot grows bad-tempered near the end of the flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pilot' looks like a flyer, but it is a trial, as in a pilot scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-tempered and easily annoyed are synonyms for this.

clue.text: Human being, unusually large and thin

indicators.note: something done unusually is done in an odd way, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A description of someone oddly built: big yet slender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges LARGE and THIN together; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: In science fiction an inhabitant of Earth, that is, a person, is called this.

clue.text: Storms making crack in roads

indicators.note: crack is placed in the middle of the abbreviation for roads

parts.note: RDS is the abbreviation for roads
crack means first-rate, A1, written here AI

explanation.surface: A storm causes a crack to open up in the roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storms' is a verb here, as in troops storming a building. Crack means top-class, A1, with the 1 written as I.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm a place is to attack it suddenly, so attacks of this kind are sudden incursions.

clue.text: Tiny new truck driven by Australian on motorway

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the following pieces come after motorway

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI
a ute is a utility truck, the Australian word for a pickup

explanation.surface: An Australian drives a small new pickup truck along the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective here, stressed on its second syllable, is a synonym for very small.

clue.text: In America, attempt to secure dollars is hard work

indicators.note: securing something holds it inside, so dollars is fixed within the opening letters

parts.note: US is short for the United States, America
D is an abbreviation for dollars
to try is to attempt

explanation.surface: A tale of chasing money in the United States, which takes effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Diligence or hard graft is one meaning of the word, beside its sense of manufacturing.

clue.text: Suddenly find me wearing short garment, far from happy

indicators.note: wearing a garment puts oneself inside it, so me goes within
short means the garment loses its last letter

parts.note: a coat is a garment
cross means angry, far from happy

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles on themselves in a short skirt, and is unhappy about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To chance upon something unexpectedly is to discover it by accident.

clue.text: Gosh — vet's mislaid lead

indicators.note: losing the lead means losing the front letter of the synonym

parts.note: to vet is to check thoroughly

explanation.surface: A veterinarian has lost the leash for a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vet' and 'lead' suggest an animal doctor and a dog's leash; vet is the verb, to check, and lead its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise or annoyance, a pair of minced oaths.

clue.text: Noble's shout of joy, swallowing tranquilliser without hesitation

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so the drug goes into the shout

parts.note: a cheer is a shout of joy

indicators.note: um is a hesitation sound, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Valium is a brand of tranquilliser

explanation.surface: An aristocrat whoops for joy as he downs a sedative in one go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without hesitation' looks like 'promptly' but strips UM from VALIUM, leaving VALI.
explanation.definitionFit: In France a knight or member of certain orders of nobility holds this rank.

clue.text: Oh! Is that how the compiler views these sweets?

definitions.text: Oh! Is that how the compiler views these sweets?

parts.words: Oh! Is that how the compiler views these sweets?
parts.note: the setter pictures sweets printed with romantic messages, and an exclamation of affection, as though the compiler adores them

explanation.surface: A rueful question about the compiler's fondness for certain sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: Love Hearts are fizzy British sweets shaped like hearts and stamped with short romantic messages.
explanation.definitionFit: These are a brand of heart-shaped confectionery carrying short affectionate slogans.

clue.text: Beastly type hanging around in various hotel bars

indicators.note: various means differing arrangements, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: A lout loitering in assorted hotel bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly type' suggests a nasty person; it is literally an animal, one that hangs from branches.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaggy Indian bear that hangs upside down from trees, an animal known for loafing.

clue.text: Recording prescribed in class

indicators.note: prescribed goes inside the class word

parts.note: a caste is a social class
set means fixed or prescribed, as in a set text

explanation.surface: A recording is a set text in the classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape cartridge on which music or speech is stored is a kind of recording.

clue.text: In France, Peter keeps girlfriend … here?

definitions.text: In France, Peter keeps girlfriend … here?

indicators.note: keeping something holds it within, so the girlfriend goes inside the French name

parts.note: Pierre is the French form of Peter
a date is a romantic partner one goes out with

explanation.surface: A Frenchman named Pierre keeps a lover somewhere discreet.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a small flat in town is where a man might keep a mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: A small second home kept for occasional stays, the kind of discreet flat a man might keep a mistress in.

clue.text: Bullets lodged in commander's back

indicators.note: back means the letters are read from right to left
something lodged in a word sits inside it, so the answer's letters are found within commander's

explanation.surface: Bullets have become lodged in an officer's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like part of the body; it says the letters found in commander's are read the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammunition, shortened informally, covers bullets and shells.

clue.text: Fellow giving daughter a look

parts.note: mien is a person's look or bearing

explanation.surface: A man casts a glance at his daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, so any fellow could bear it.

clue.text: Female's account in court: it's impressive

indicators.note: the female and account pieces are placed within the abbreviation for court

parts.note: a lass is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A woman gives her testimony in court, and it is impressive.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer or thing of real quality, something that stands out as excellent.

clue.text: Drink up quietly in empty cafeteria

indicators.note: the pieces go within what is left of the cafeteria
emptying a word leaves only its outside letters

parts.note: p, piano, means quietly in music

explanation.surface: Someone drinks up quietly in a deserted café.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea, a hot drink.

clue.text: Ready to welcome sailor back in part of North African city

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them inside, so the sailor goes into ready money

parts.note: the ready is slang for cash

indicators.note: back means the sailor's letters run the other way

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone stands prepared to greet a returning seaman in a North African city.
explanation.definitionFit: The old walled citadel quarter of a North African city such as Algiers bears this name.

clue.text: Skirmish in Civil War botched up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
the answer sits inside the words Civil War botched

explanation.surface: A fight in a badly handled civil war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'botched up' looks like a phrase meaning ruined; 'up' turns the letters found in Civil War botched.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy fight or scuffle is close in sense to a minor clash.

clue.text: Starts to fidget in long motion picture

indicators.note: the starts of the words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Someone starts to squirm during a lengthy movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motion picture' looks like one phrase; 'motion' gives a letter and 'picture' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is an informal word for a movie, as in going to the pictures.

clue.text: Maybe coat isn't needed after second of April

indicators.note: the colloquial word for isn't comes after that letter
the second letter of April is the one taken

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: Come April, perhaps a coat isn't required any more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' looks like a garment, but it is a layer of paint, so 'Maybe' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat of emulsion or gloss is an example of the stuff applied to walls.

clue.text: Start to speak about soldier returning home

indicators.note: about puts the speaking word around the soldier and home pieces

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally

indicators.note: returning means the soldier's letters run backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone begins to talk about a soldier coming back home.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin or arise is to come into being, a synonym of starting.

clue.text: Stuffy person with no children dying thus, you say?

indicators.note: you say means the clue is said out loud, so a word heard the same is wanted

parts.words: person with no children dying thus
parts.note: someone dying childless dies without heirs, heirless

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how a childless person dies.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffy room lacks fresh ventilation, close and unventilated.

clue.text: Left in cattle trough, one causes great damage

indicators.note: left is put inside the trough word

parts.note: a manger is a feeding trough for cattle

explanation.surface: Something left in a cattle trough does terrible harm.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something that mangles, crushing or mutilating badly, is a destroyer.
